scenes.title: Basic Tastes
scenes.text: Your tongue detects five basic tastes, but almost all flavor actually comes from your sense of smell.

scenes.title: Chili
scenes.text: Chili is not a taste but pain. Capsaicin tricks your mouth into feeling heat that is not there.

scenes.title: Sound
scenes.text: Crisp food tastes better because your brain uses the crunch sound to judge freshness and quality.

scenes.title: Ice Cream
scenes.text: Cold numbs your taste buds, which is why ice cream needs far more sugar to taste sweet.

scenes.title: Rising
scenes.text: Bread rises because yeast eats sugar and releases gas, trapping bubbles inside the soft dough.

scenes.title: Searing
scenes.text: The brown crust on meat comes from a chemical reaction creating hundreds of new flavor molecules.

scenes.title: Memory
scenes.text: Food tastes tie to memory stronger than almost anything, which is why a smell can take you home.

scenes.title: Your Turn
scenes.text: Every bite is chemistry and memory combined. What food instantly takes you back to childhood?
